$comment: Single source of truth for Nylon's design tokens. Run `bun run tokens` after editing; it regenerates src/web/src/styles/tokens.css and the iOS Theme.swift. `bun run tokens:check` (part of `bun run lint`) fails when those are stale. A colour may add `highContrast` (light and dark) for Increase Contrast: iOS uses it, and web maps it to `prefers-contrast: more`. A colour may add `alpha` (0–1), which applies to every one of its values, or `{ light, dark }` for one per appearance. See 'Visual language' in https://github.com/superhighfives/nylon-impossible/blob/02f8c45b3ba52896a25bde813cfd2b0a05ef9fb1/plans/done/2026-10-18-cohesive-redesign.md.

surface.usage: Raised areas: sheets (the wide board's open todo included), the composer (hover and focus), the drag preview, Done's tint

fill.usage: Soft fills: chips, selected rows; 60% for row hover

hairline.usage: Every divider, 1px/1pt, drawn once: between columns, the header and toolbar rules, the sidebar edge

ink.usage: Primary text; the sidebar's bar for the column holding the selection; 20% for the soft keyboard focus tint

inkMuted.usage: Secondary text, meta line, a selected row's keyboard bar

sectionOutline.usage: The 4pt outline inside the wide board's section with the keyboard (the sidebar, a column, the open todo). A frame, not a selection; never brand

notice.usage: Overnight note text and icons, on noticeFill

brand.usage: Fills: done checkbox, send button, a sidebar list as a drop target, the drop line's dot, a due-today chip, the toast's pill (bar an error's), the overnight note. Thin lines only for the two Settled exceptions: the drop line while dragging and the composer's focus ring. Never text on white.

brandInk.usage: Text, icons and outlines on a brand fill: the toast's outline action and its focus ring

brandSoft.source: yellow-9 at 22% (16% in dark, where 22% over canvas reads as olive)
brandSoft.usage: The gap a touch drag opens between the rows it parts. A fill, never a line or text

type.$comment: Both apps read these. Each style is a role, named for what it sets: its size and lineHeight in px/pt, weight (100–900), tracking in em (0 when absent) and font (a key of `font`). The web gets one Tailwind utility per role, `text-n-<density>-<role>` (`text-n-wide-row-title`), which sets all four; `font-n-display` still sets the family. Apple gets the roles with an iosTextStyle, which Dynamic Type scales them by, as `Theme.Fonts.Phone.rowTitle`. `phone` is the iPhone and the web's phone layout; `wide` the Mac popover, the web's wide board and the web's pages and dialogs outside it, at every width; `landing` the web's landing page. Roles without an iosTextStyle are sizes only the web draws, kept at their size until a design pass collapses them. codeScale sizes code in the notes, inline and in blocks, against the notes' own type, since a monospace face at the same size is wider and taller; the web reads it as --n-type-code-scale.

body.usage: Notes, settings rows and the composer (Apple); the composer (web)

rowTitle.usage: A todo's title in a row

control.usage: Switcher titles, quiet buttons, the calendar's month

subtask.usage: Subtask titles in the detail sheet (Apple)

action.usage: The web's quiet buttons: back, Try again, Delete

secondary.usage: The web's secondary lines: counts, the detail rows, the calendar's days

item.usage: The web's settings rows, menu items, and subtasks and their fields

button.usage: The web's account rows and Sign out

emptyLine.usage: The web's empty line, at a row's size

code.usage: The web's API token, in a monospace face

title.usage: Collection names (Apple); dialog titles and the Gmail connect pages (web)

body.usage: Body copy: the composer, menus, the palette, toasts

rowTitle.usage: A todo's title in a row

metaChip.usage: A meta chip's label (Apple reads the phone's)

notes.usage: The web's notes, subtasks and empty lines, on a row's line

control.usage: The web's filled buttons and strong sidebar entries

action.usage: The web's quiet buttons and sidebar entries

groupLabel.usage: The web's sidebar and palette group labels

pageTitle.usage: The web's error, not found and legal titles

lede.usage: The web's error and not found copy

secondary.usage: The web's pages outside the board: legal dates, the Gmail connect copy

secondaryStrong.usage: The web's offline banner and the Gmail connect button

code.usage: The web's API docs code blocks

space.$comment: Apple reads these. The web doesn't: it uses Tailwind's default spacing, whose 4px step matches this scale, so tokens.css doesn't emit them.

sheet.$comment: The open todo on the web's wide board: a sheet as wide as a column, laid on the board after its todo's column. It overlaps that column by `overlap`, which is the column's own right padding, so opening it never rewraps the column's text. The column recedes to `recede` opacity, bar the selected row. The shadow is ink-black at `shadowOpacity`, cast left.

board.$comment: The web's wide board columns: each a third of the board, so Today, This week and Someday fill it, from `columnMinWidth` up to `columnMaxWidth`. Only a board wider than three columns at `columnMaxWidth` leaves room past the last list, before Done; that room, which a `hairline` closes, is a hatch of `hairline` lines at `opacity`, `width` thick, `spacing` apart, at `angle` degrees. The web draws it from a square tile `spacing` × √2 wide, rounded to a whole pixel, so the lines can't band; that only holds at 45°. The section with the keyboard (the sidebar, a column, the open todo) is framed inside its edges by a `sectionOutlineWidth` line of `sectionOutline`.

motion.$comment: A dragged todo tilts by one angle per drag, picked at random between -tiltMax and +tiltMax degrees when it lifts, and scales to `lift`. It gets there over `fast`, overshooting to `tiltOvershoot` times the angle at 60%. The landed row swings `settleOvershoot` degrees past level, the opposite way to its tilt, at 60%, unless it was tilted less than `settleMinTilt` degrees. Reduced motion keeps the tilt as a still pose and drops the overshoot and the swing.

icons.$comment: lucide (web) → SF Symbol (iOS), so the same glyph means the same thing. Add both sides when either app needs a new icon.
